clips.text_en_b1: In 2021 he was 22 and made random crypto money from dogecoin. He lived two years with no job, dropped out of school, and bought a condo for $230K. Then money ran out. He went back, graduated, and now makes $100K at 27. Stuck in a loop of work and consume, with student debt and credit card debt.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon lost his crypto gains, now trapped in the grind

signal.rationale: Anon's story is a cautionary tale, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2021, when he was 22, this guy stumbled into a small fortune after throwing money at dogecoin on a whim. For roughly two years he coasted along with no real job, dropped out of school, and splashed $230K on a condo. Once the windfall dried up, though, he had to swallow his pride, return to finish his degree, and land a $100K salary at 27. Now he's stuck grinding through debt payments, buried under student loans and credit card bills.
clips.text_en_c1: At 22, he had the kind of windfall most people only daydream about: a speculative dogecoin position that paid out handsomely during the 2021 surge. Flush with cash, he dropped out of university, blew through two years of leisure, and put $230,000 down on a condominium. The party, however, was not meant to last. Once the money evaporated, reality came knocking. He eventually re-enrolled, finished his degree, and now, at 27, earns a respectable $100K salary. Yet the gloss has worn off entirely. He is burdened by lingering student loans and credit card debt, trapped in the familiar grind-to-consume cycle.
clips.text_en_c2: In 2021, at twenty-two, he parlayed an evidently fortuitous windfall on Dogecoin into a life of ostentatious leisure: two years of abstaining from any gainful employment, an abandoned academic trajectory, and the acquisition of a condominium valued at roughly $230,000. When the capital evaporated, necessity reasserted itself with rather brutal clarity. He re-enrolled, eventually graduated, and now, at twenty-seven, draws a respectable $100,000 salary, yet remains tethered to outstanding student loans and revolving credit card balances, ensnared in what he himself characterised as an interminable work-and-consume cycle. Having once sampled the headier pleasures of unfettered affluence, he confesses an unwillingness to relinquish them, and the entire trajectory reads as an object lesson in how fleeting, speculative gains tend to recalibrate one's expectations in ways that subsequent, conventional prosperity can seldom satisfy.

clips.text_en_b1: Anyone else fed up with Musk trying to get shit to trend on 4chan? He pumps money into AfD and still can't break 50% of the vote. The guy only got rich because his daddy's mining money let him in. X is just Musk crying into the void asking people to boost his posts.

clips.text_en_b2: Is anyone else thoroughly fed up with Musk trying to manipulate what trends on 4chan? Despite pumping serious cash into AfD, the party still can't crack 50% of the vote. The bloke only got filthy rich because daddy's mining empire handed him the keys. Meanwhile X is basically Musk screaming into the void, begging randoms to boost his engagement. A lot of it stinks like paid astroturfing and completely broken metrics. Honestly, between the astroturfing and the desperate self-promotion, the whole operation reeks.
clips.text_en_c1: It is becoming increasingly tiresome to watch Musk perpetually attempting to manipulate trends across forums. He lavishes funds on Germany's AfD, yet the party still cannot breach the 50 percent threshold that would actually matter. His fortune, in truth, owes far more to inherited emerald mining capital than to any genuine business acumen. The platform formerly known as Twitter has devolved into little more than a megaphone for his grievances, a place where he pleads with users to amplify his posts. Much of the engagement appears suspiciously manufactured—bot traffic, inflated metrics, the whole charade.
clips.text_en_c2: It is scarcely surprising that seasoned traders recognise the now-familiar choreography: whenever Dogecoin registers an appreciable surge, one can almost invariably trace the catalyst to a single, opportune missive from Elon Musk. Astute operators have, accordingly, refined their playbook to a principle of studied passivity, awaiting his post before committing capital, lest they be left acquiring at the apex. The present author confesses, somewhat ruefully, to still being ensnared in such a position, the loss constituting yet another instalment in what can only be described as an ongoing, prohibitively expensive tuition. Whether this constitutes market intelligence or merely the latest instalment in a personal finance cautionary tale remains, perhaps, a matter of perspective. Source: 4chan /pol/.

clips.text_en_b2: On September 8th, OpenAI revealed that their model Astra, running on GPT-6, had cracked a notoriously difficult math problem, burning through roughly $20 million in compute along the way. Shortly afterwards, researcher Tristan Buckmaster pointed out that OpenAI's approach bore a striking resemblance to his own ongoing work, which he had been developing with the help of OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude. The leaked video suggests a genuine ethical conflict over unattributed use of someone's research.
clips.text_en_c1: On September 8th, OpenAI made headlines by announcing that their Astra model, built atop GPT-6, had cracked an exceptionally difficult mathematical problem—an achievement that reportedly consumed roughly $20 million in compute resources. Almost immediately, however, trouble surfaced. Researcher Tristan Buckmaster publicly observed that the methodology bore a striking resemblance to work he had been pursuing with OpenAI's own Codex and Anthropic's Claude. A leaked video subsequently alleged that OpenAI had absorbed substantial portions of his research without due attribution. If true, this would constitute a serious ethical breach and raise uncomfortable questions about the extent to which frontier AI laboratories appropriate the intellectual labour of independent academics.
clips.text_en_c2: OpenAI disclosed on the eighth of September that their forthcoming model, Astra, operating on the GPT-6 architecture, had successfully resolved a particularly intractable mathematical problem, an undertaking that reportedly consumed approximately twenty million dollars in computational expenditure. Almost immediately, however, the researcher Tristan Buckmaster publicly noted that the methodology bore a rather conspicuous resemblance to work he had himself been cultivating, notably with assistance from OpenAI's own Codex system and Anthropic's Claude. The accompanying video documentation appears to allege a substantive ethical conflict concerning unacknowledged appropriation of intellectual contributions, and the affair has predictably ignited fervent debate regarding the increasingly porous boundaries between collaborative iteration and outright plagiarism within the contemporary artificial intelligence research ecosystem.

clips.text_zh: OECD PISA 760K學生91國 全球數學閱讀跌 中國平均612 已經等於其他國家精英級 香港都唔得啦 wtf
clips.text_en_b1: A new OECD PISA study tested 760,000 students across 91 countries and global scores in math and reading comprehension are dropping. Except in China. The average Chinese kid scored 612, which is already above the elite level 5 threshold of 607 that marks top performers in the rest of the world. Normal Chinese students sit at a level considered elite elsewhere.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on China dominating new PISA results
clips.text_en_b2: A fresh OECD PISA study, which tested around 760,000 students across 91 countries, found that global scores in math and reading comprehension are steadily declining — except in China. The average Chinese student scored 612, which already clears the elite Level 5 threshold of 607, a benchmark that essentially marks top-tier performance elsewhere in the world. In other words, a run-of-the-mill kid in China is performing at what other countries would consider an elite level.
clips.text_en_c1: The latest OECD PISA assessment, which surveyed 760,000 students across 91 countries, has delivered a sobering verdict on global educational standards: mathematical literacy and reading comprehension have both declined across most regions. There is, however, one conspicuous exception. Chinese students averaged 612, a figure that exceeds the 607 threshold defining the elite Level 5 tier, which elsewhere is reached only by the top-performing percentile. In other words, a representative Chinese pupil now performs at a level considered exceptional throughout the rest of the world. The implications for universities and employers in the West are rather disquieting, particularly given that even Hong Kong's once-dominant results have begun to slip.
clips.text_en_c2: The most recent OECD Programme for International Student Assessment administered its rigorous battery of evaluations to approximately 760,000 students distributed across ninety-one participating nations, and the aggregate findings are, by most measures, disquieting: global competencies in both mathematics and reading comprehension have registered a discernible decline, a trajectory that has occasioned considerable hand-wringing among educational policymakers. China constitutes the conspicuous exception to this otherwise bleak tendency, with the mean Chinese student achieving a score of 612, comfortably eclipsing the elite Level 5 threshold of 607 that demarcates top-tier performance throughout the remainder of the surveyed world. What elsewhere qualifies as exceptional attainment is, for the average Chinese pupil, merely the baseline, a distinction that inevitably provokes uncomfortable questions about pedagogical methodology and curricular rigour elsewhere.

clips.text_en_b2: I'm currently chasing the classic 1/2/3/4 strength standard: a one-plate overhead press, two-plate bench, three-plate squat, and four-plate deadlift. At the moment, I'm noticeably closer to grinding out a one-plate OHP than I am to hitting the other three milestones. clips.text_en_c1: I have been steadily pursuing what gym circles typically refer to as the 1/2/3/4 benchmark: a one-plate overhead press, a two-plate bench press, a three-plate squat, and a four-plate deadlift. At present, however, I find myself lagging considerably across most of these milestones. My overhead press is hovering tantalisingly close to a single plate for reps, whereas my bench remains stubbornly short of two plates and my squat and deadlift are still some way off their respective targets. Realistically, I anticipate hitting that one-plate OHP within a month or two of consistent training. The remaining lifts will require substantially more patience and considerably more food.
clips.text_en_c2: One pursues, with measured if perhaps quixotic ambition, the venerable 1/2/3/4 standard beloved of strength-training enthusiasts: a one-plate overhead press, a two-plate bench, a three-plate squat, and a four-plate deadlift, an ostensibly modest benchmark that nevertheless proves elusive in practice. At present, the one-plate overhead press represents the most attainable milestone, whilst the squat and deadlift remain, lamentably, rather more distant objectives upon the horizon. A single-plate overhead press for repetitions appears plausibly achievable within a month or two of concerted effort, assuming reasonable continuity of training and nutritional discipline. The remaining lifts, however, shall require rather more protracted cultivation, and one's more generously proportioned acquaintances continue, with predictable hilarity, to remark upon the comparatively diminutive proportions currently exhibited.

clips.text_zh: Walpurgis no Kaiten訪問raw同漫畫第一期都流咗出嚟 Homura聲優Chiwa Saito話Muhdoka係Homura初戀 WTF 巴哈膠晒
clips.text_en_b1: The Kaiten interview raws and the manga adaptation volume 01 of Puella Magica Madoka: Walpurgis no Kaiten are out. Volume 1 of the manga is already being shared online. Chiwa Saito, Homura's voice actress, said in an interview that Muhdoka is Homura's first love. The old fanbase is melting down about it.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on new Madoka Magica project leaks
clips.text_en_b2: The raw interview transcripts for Walpurgis no Kaiten have leaked online, alongside scans of the manga adaptation's first volume for Puella Magica Madoka. Fans have already been sharing volume one across various boards. In a particularly eyebrow-raising moment from the interview, Chiwa Saito, Homura's voice actress, casually dropped that Muhdoka is essentially Homura's first love. Predictably, the veteran fanbase has completely lost it, with threads melting down over the implications.
clips.text_en_c1: Both the raw transcript of the Walpurgis no Kaiten production interview and the inaugural volume of its manga adaptation have now surfaced online, much to the delight of curious fans. The leak has, predictably, set the community ablaze, particularly because Chiwa Saito—Homura's longtime voice actress—dropped a rather incendiary revelation during the conversation. She disclosed that the character Muhdoka is, in her own characterisation, Homura's first love, a narrative development that has prompted considerable hand-wringing among the veteran fanbase. Whether this constitutes elegant world-building or a gratuitous subversion of established canon depends very much on whom you ask. The forums, predictably, have descended into absolute pandemonium.
clips.text_en_c2: The preliminary interview transcripts pertaining to Walpurgis no Kaiten, alongside the inaugural volume of its accompanying manga adaptation of Puella Magica Madoka, have, somewhat prematurely, found their way into wider circulation, occasioning considerable perturbation amongst the established fan community. Volume one of the manga in particular has proliferated with what can only be described as alacrity. Chiwa Saito, the esteemed voice actress entrusted with the portrayal of Homura, reportedly articulated during the interview that Muhdoka constitutes Homura's inaugural romantic attachment, a revelation that has predictably induced a rather spectacular collective meltdown amongst longstanding enthusiasts. Whether this constitutes a substantive narrative development or merely a provocation designed to destabilise the faithful remains a matter of considerable interpretive contention.
